item.title: Blue Wahoos Stay Hot, Edge Closer to Division Crown
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Pensacola Blue Wahoos kept their winning streak alive Saturday night with a 5-2 victory over the Montgomery Biscuits, moving within striking distance of the South Division second half championship. The win marked the Blue Wahoos' third straight triumph and reduced their magic number to six games as they pursue the divisional title. The team's…
item.content:encoded:
The Pensacola Blue Wahoos kept their winning streak alive Saturday night with a 5-2 victory over the Montgomery Biscuits, moving within striking distance of the South Division second half championship.

The win marked the Blue Wahoos' third straight triumph and reduced their magic number to six games as they pursue the divisional title. The team's momentum heading into the final stretch of the season suggests they're hitting their stride at a critical time.

According to reporting from North Escambia, the Blue Wahoos set a home run record in the victory, though specifics on that mark weren't immediately detailed. The offensive outburst proved the difference against the Biscuits in what was a solid all-around performance for the Pensacola squad.

item.title: Florida Weighs AI Rules for College Students, Vaccine Requirements
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: As students settle into the new school year, Florida education officials are grappling with how to regulate artificial intelligence use on college campuses, while state health authorities are pushing to reduce the number of vaccines required for school attendance. The dual policy discussions reflect broader debates playing out across Florida's…
item.content:encoded:
As students settle into the new school year, Florida education officials are grappling with how to regulate artificial intelligence use on college campuses, while state health authorities are pushing to reduce the number of vaccines required for school attendance.

The dual policy discussions reflect broader debates playing out across Florida's education system. College administrators and educators say they need clear guidelines on when and how students can use AI tools in coursework, as the technology becomes increasingly prevalent in academic settings.

Meanwhile, health officials have suggested loosening vaccine requirements currently mandated for students to enroll in schools. The proposal has drawn attention as states nationwide reconsider immunization policies in the post-pandemic era.

Both issues are expected to see further discussion as the Florida Legislature prepares for upcoming sessions and education boards consider regulatory changes.

item.title: FWC Offers Free Hunter Safety Courses Across North Escambia in September
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission is hosting free hunter safety courses throughout North Escambia County this month, with classroom sessions scheduled in Molino, Cantonment, Jay, and Milton. The courses are designed to teach students proper hunting safety practices, conservation principles, and responsible hunting habits.…
item.content:encoded:
The Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission is hosting free hunter safety courses throughout North Escambia County this month, with classroom sessions scheduled in Molino, Cantonment, Jay, and Milton.

The courses are designed to teach students proper hunting safety practices, conservation principles, and responsible hunting habits. Participants can complete the online portion of the course at their own pace before attending an in-person class session in their area.

According to the FWC, hunter safety certification is required for anyone born after June 1, 1975 who wants to hunt in Florida. The courses cover firearm safety, hunting regulations, wildlife management, and ethical hunting practices.

Interested hunters can register online at the FWC website and choose their preferred class location. More details about specific dates and times for the North Escambia sessions are available through the FWC's hunter safety program page.

item.title: I-10 Resurfacing Work Causes Traffic Delays in Escambia County

item.content:encoded:
Drivers heading through Escambia County should expect slowdowns on Interstate 10 as resurfacing work continues east of U.S. 231, according to a weekly traffic report from the Florida Department of Transportation.

The ongoing construction project is part of routine maintenance to keep the major corridor in working condition. Crews are actively working on the roadway, which means motorists should anticipate reduced speeds and possible lane closures during daylight hours.

Travelers are urged to allow extra time for their commutes and remain alert in work zones. Alternative routes may be available depending on your destination, so checking real-time traffic conditions before heading out is recommended.

For the most up-to-date information on construction timelines and potential delays, drivers can check the FDOT website or local traffic reports.

item.title: Century Inmate Gets Extra Prison Time for Trafficking Meth Behind Bars
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: An inmate at Century Correctional Institution has been convicted and sentenced to additional prison time after authorities discovered a substantial amount of methamphetamine and other contraband during a routine search. The discovery highlighted ongoing challenges with drug trafficking within correctional facilities in Escambia County. The inmate…
item.content:encoded:
An inmate at Century Correctional Institution has been convicted and sentenced to additional prison time after authorities discovered a substantial amount of methamphetamine and other contraband during a routine search.

The discovery highlighted ongoing challenges with drug trafficking within correctional facilities in Escambia County. The inmate was found with what investigators determined was a trafficking quantity of methamphetamine, leading to additional charges beyond his original sentence.

Century Correctional Institution, located in North Escambia County, continues to work with law enforcement to prevent contraband from entering the facility and to maintain security within the prison. The case underscores the persistent problem of drug smuggling in Florida's corrections system, where inmates and outside collaborators frequently attempt to bring controlled substances into facilities.

item.title: Scattered Thunderstorms Expected Sunday, Heat Continues
item.dc:creator: newsroom

The National Weather Service forecasts a 40 percent chance of showers and thunderstorms developing after 10 a.m., with partly sunny skies expected otherwise. Winds will start light from the east before…
item.content:encoded:
The Pensacola area is in for a typical summer day Sunday, with afternoon thunderstorms possible and temperatures climbing toward 90 degrees. The National Weather Service forecasts a 40 percent chance of showers and thunderstorms developing after 10 a.m., with partly sunny skies expected otherwise. Winds will start light from the east before shifting south during the afternoon.

Sunday night should clear out somewhat, with partly cloudy conditions and a low around 72 degrees. Residents heading out early in the day should have clear conditions, but those planning afternoon activities may want to keep an eye on developing storm chances. The heat and humidity will remain typical for this time of year across the Escambia and Santa Rosa County areas.

item.title: Frontier Ending Copper Landline Service Across North Escambia Communities
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Frontier Communications is phasing out traditional copper-based landline phone service in several Northwest Florida communities, including Walnut Hill, Molino, and Bratt, as well as parts of Alabama near Atmore. The telecommunications company has already secured FCC approval for the service discontinuation in Alabama. A similar application to…
item.content:encoded:
Frontier Communications is phasing out traditional copper-based landline phone service in several Northwest Florida communities, including Walnut Hill, Molino, and Bratt, as well as parts of Alabama near Atmore.

The telecommunications company has already secured FCC approval for the service discontinuation in Alabama. A similar application to retire legacy telephone infrastructure in Frontier's Florida service area is moving through the federal approval process.

Residents and businesses still relying on Frontier's copper landlines in these areas will need to transition to alternative phone services. Frontier has been gradually shifting customers toward fiber-optic and digital alternatives as part of a broader industry trend away from aging copper infrastructure. Customers affected by the change should contact Frontier directly to explore available service options in their area.

item.title: Mobile's Crafts and Drafts Market Connects Local Vendors With Shoppers
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A monthly market in downtown Mobile is creating opportunities for small business owners to connect directly with customers while giving shoppers a chance to support local vendors. Crafts and Drafts returned to Oyster City Brewing Company on Saturday evening, according to WKRG News 5, drawing crowds from 5 to 9 p.m. The recurring event has become a…
item.content:encoded: A monthly market in downtown Mobile is creating opportunities for small business owners to connect directly with customers while giving shoppers a chance to support local vendors. Crafts and Drafts returned to Oyster City Brewing Company on Saturday evening, according to WKRG News 5, drawing crowds from 5 to 9 p.m. The recurring event has become a popular gathering spot in the area, combining the appeal of handmade goods with the casual atmosphere of a local brewery. For small business owners in the Mobile area, the market provides a lower-cost way to test products, build brand awareness, and establish relationships with repeat customers without the overhead of a permanent retail location. The event also gives shoppers an alternative to chain retailers, offering unique, locally-made items while supporting entrepreneurs in their community.

item.content:encoded: The City of Prichard dealt with a water main break Friday afternoon that affected a major service area, according to the Prichard Public Services Department. Details on the specific location of the break and the scope of the service disruption were limited in the initial announcement. The incident underscores ongoing challenges with aging water infrastructure in the region. Residents in the affected area were advised to monitor local updates from the Prichard Public Services Department for information on restoration efforts and any boil-water notices.

item.content:encoded:
The MoonPie Over Mobile New Year celebration is building anticipation with a countdown timer to reveal the main musical acts that will headline the popular Gulf Coast event as revelers prepare to ring in 2027.

The annual celebration, held in Mobile, Alabama, draws thousands of visitors to downtown for its iconic MoonPie drop and live entertainment. Organizers have made a practice of keeping headliner announcements suspenseful, releasing performers in stages leading up to the final event.

While specific dates and performer names haven't yet been released, fans of the celebration can expect details to roll out in the coming weeks as the countdown progresses. The event remains one of the region's largest New Year's Eve gatherings.

item.content:encoded:
A busy night of high school football across the North Escambia area saw several dominant performances Friday, with Northview routing McIntosh 42-13 and Jay overwhelming Elberta 56-8.

Tate edged Milton in a closer contest, 24-21, while Pensacola High dominated Gulf Breeze 32-10. Pine Forest and Escambia battled to a scoreless tie through regulation.

In other action, Niceville defeated West Florida 41-14 on Thursday, and Washington rolled past Navarre 45-27. Pace got past Catholic 33-21 to round out the week's results across the region.

item.title: Undefeated Northview Chiefs Head East to Face Graceville After Dominant Win
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Northview Chiefs stayed perfect on the season Friday night with a commanding 42-13 victory over McIntosh, pushing their record to 2-0 with an impressive road performance just across the state line in Washington County, Alabama. The dominant showing sets up another significant road test for the North Escambia program. Northview will travel…
item.content:encoded:
The Northview Chiefs stayed perfect on the season Friday night with a commanding 42-13 victory over McIntosh, pushing their record to 2-0 with an impressive road performance just across the state line in Washington County, Alabama.

The dominant showing sets up another significant road test for the North Escambia program. Northview will travel roughly 140 miles east next week to take on the Graceville Tigers in what figures to be another challenging non-conference matchup early in the season.

The Chiefs have now won both of their early-season contests away from home, suggesting head coach Mike Cokley's squad is building confidence as a unit. The back-to-back road games should provide valuable experience before conference play gets underway.

item.content:encoded:
Senior quarterback Cade Pierce had a homecoming to remember Friday night, leading the Tate Aggies to a hard-fought 24-21 road victory over his former team, the Milton Panthers.

Pierce, who previously played for Milton before transferring to Tate, delivered when it mattered most in the North Escambia matchup. The Aggies' offense proved just enough to hold off a Panthers team that kept the game close throughout.

The victory keeps Tate competitive in what's shaping up to be an active Friday night football season across the Pensacola area. Pierce's performance against his former program adds another chapter to what's becoming an interesting storyline in local high school sports.

item.title: Escambia County Fire Rescue Trains for Grain Bin Rescue Operations
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Escambia County Fire Rescue participated in specialized training this week alongside the Jay Fire Department to prepare crews for one of agriculture's most dangerous emergencies: grain bin entrapment rescues. The Grain Bin Rescue Class tested firefighters' technical skills in handling situations that pose unique hazards. Grain bin incidents are…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County Fire Rescue participated in specialized training this week alongside the Jay Fire Department to prepare crews for one of agriculture's most dangerous emergencies: grain bin entrapment rescues.

The Grain Bin Rescue Class tested firefighters' technical skills in handling situations that pose unique hazards. Grain bin incidents are among the most challenging rescue scenarios first responders face, requiring specialized knowledge and equipment to safely extract victims who can become trapped in flowing grain or other agricultural materials.

The joint training between ECFR and Jay Fire Department reflects the region's commitment to ensuring emergency personnel are equipped to handle agricultural emergencies. North Escambia remains a significant agricultural area, making such specialized preparedness crucial for rural fire departments.

item.content:encoded:
A wet weather pattern is moving into the North Escambia region this weekend, with rain chances increasing as we move into early next week.

Saturday looks mostly dry through the morning, but scattered showers and thunderstorms are expected to develop after 1 p.m., according to the National Weather Service. There's a 30 percent chance of precipitation, with temperatures reaching near 88 degrees and light winds.

The picture becomes wetter on Sunday and Monday, when showers and thunderstorms are forecast to become more likely across the area. If you're planning outdoor activities, Saturday morning and early afternoon would be your best window before conditions deteriorate. Make sure to keep an eye on the forecast as the weekend progresses.

item.title: Century Council Members Join State League of Cities Policy Committees
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Two members of the Century Town Council have been tapped to serve on Florida League of Cities policy committees for the coming two years, bringing local input to statewide municipal discussions. Councilwoman Shelisa McCall Abraham will serve on the Development, Code Compliance, and Redevelopment Committee, while Councilmember Sparkie Harrison has…
item.content:encoded:
Two members of the Century Town Council have been tapped to serve on Florida League of Cities policy committees for the coming two years, bringing local input to statewide municipal discussions.

Councilwoman Shelisa McCall Abraham will serve on the Development, Code Compliance, and Redevelopment Committee, while Councilmember Sparkie Harrison has been appointed to the Finance and Taxation Committee. Both will represent the town on the Legislative Policy Committees through 2027.

The appointments reflect Century's engagement with the Florida League of Cities, a statewide organization that advocates for municipal interests during legislative sessions and helps shape policy on issues affecting local governments across the state.

item.content:encoded:
Drivers in North Escambia should expect significant traffic disruptions starting today as work crews close a major stretch of West Roberts Road for ongoing reconstruction and drainage improvements.

The closure affects West Roberts Road between Tate Road and Highway 29 as part of a $4.6 million roadway improvement project. According to the project timeline, the road is expected to reopen after Labor Day weekend, weather permitting.

Commuters in the area should plan alternate routes during the closure. The improvements aim to upgrade both the roadway itself and the drainage infrastructure along that corridor.

item.title: DeSantis Reappoints Nick Patronis to NW Florida Water Board
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Gov. Ron DeSantis has announced the reappointment of Nick Patronis to the Northwest Florida Water Management District Governing Board, according to reporting from NorthEscambia.com. Patronis, whose brother U.S. Rep. Jimmy Patronis represents Florida's 1st Congressional District, will continue serving on the nine-member governing board that…
item.content:encoded:
Gov. Ron DeSantis has announced the reappointment of Nick Patronis to the Northwest Florida Water Management District Governing Board, according to reporting from NorthEscambia.com. Patronis, whose brother U.S. Rep. Jimmy Patronis represents Florida's 1st Congressional District, will continue serving on the nine-member governing board that oversees water management for the region.

This marks Patronis' fifth appointment to the board, indicating a long tenure in the role overseeing water policy and resource management for Northwest Florida. The water management district handles critical issues affecting local water supply, conservation, and environmental stewardship across the region including Escambia and Santa Rosa counties.

Jimmy Patronis, who previously served as Florida's Chief Financial Officer, was elected to Congress in 2022 and now represents the Panhandle district. The reappointment continues the family's involvement in state and local governance.
